# Secure Environment Manager (SEM V2) — Complete Technical Reference

> Authoritative architectural specification, API reference, cryptographic security model, and integration documentation for Secure Environment Manager (SEM V2).

- Canonical Domain: https://sem.niranjansah87.com.np
- Technical Documentation: https://sem.niranjansah87.com.np/docs
- Source Code: https://github.com/niranjansah87/Secure-Enviornment-Manager
- Primary Author: Niranjan Sah (https://niranjansah87.com.np)
- License: MIT License

---

## 1. System Architecture

```
Client Tier:
  ├── Next.js 15 Web Console (port 3000)
  ├── Headless CLI (@sem/cli)
  └── TypeScript SDK (@sem/sdk)
        │ (HTTPS / ES256 JWT)
        ▼
Ingress Tier: Nginx / Caddy Reverse Proxy
        │
        ▼
Application Tier: NestJS 10 + Fastify Engine (@sem/api, port 3001)
  ├── Multi-Tenant Guard (Org Isolation at Query Level)
  ├── ES256 ECDSA P-256 JWT Authentication
  ├── Cryptographic Domain (@sem/crypto)
  │     ├── Master Encryption Key (MEK) [via SEM_MASTER_KEY]
  │     ├── Project Key Encryption Key (KEK) [AES-256-GCM wrapped]
  │     └── Environment Data Encryption Key (DEK) [AES-256-GCM wrapped]
  ├── Audit Service (Append-only tamper-evident logs)
  └── Redis 7 + BullMQ Worker (@sem/worker) [Key rotation & metrics]
        │
        ▼
Persistence Tier: PostgreSQL 16 + Drizzle ORM
```

---

## 2. Cryptographic Envelope Architecture (NIST SP 800-38D)

SEM V2 eliminates plaintext storage across all layers:

1. **Master Encryption Key (MEK):**
   - 256-bit cryptographically secure key supplied via `SEM_MASTER_KEY` environment variable.
   - Master key never touches raw application secret values.
2. **Key Encryption Key (KEK):**
   - Unique per-project AES-256 key, encrypted using the MEK via AES-256-GCM.
3. **Data Encryption Key (DEK):**
   - Unique per-environment AES-256 key, encrypted using the project KEK via AES-256-GCM.
4. **Secret Plaintext Encryption:**
   - Secrets are encrypted with the environment DEK using AES-256-GCM with a unique 96-bit initialization vector (IV) per record.
5. **Additional Authenticated Data (AAD):**
   - Authentication tag verification incorporates cryptographic AAD composed of `org_id:project_id:environment_id`.
   - Prevents ciphertext relocation attacks across projects or environments.

---

## 3. Authentication & Authorization

All protected endpoints require an ES256 signed JWT in the HTTP request:
```http
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
```

### 3.1 `POST /api/v1/auth/login`
Authenticates user, admin, or scoped API key.

**Request Formats:**
```json
// Mode 1: Master Token
{ "master_token": "..." }

// Mode 2: Username & Password
{ "organization": "default", "username": "admin", "password": "..." }

// Mode 3: Scoped API Key
{ "api_key": "sem_live_..." }
```

**Response (Standard JSON Envelope):**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJFUzI1NiIs...",
    "refresh_token": "...",
    "token_type": "Bearer",
    "expires_in": 900
  }
}
```

### 3.2 `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh`
Rotates refresh tokens and issues fresh 15-minute access tokens.

---

## 4. Secrets Management API Reference

### 4.1 List Secret Metadata
```http
GET /api/v1/projects/:projectId/environments/:environmentId/secrets
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
```
Returns list of secret keys, version numbers, and update timestamps. Plaintexts are never returned in list endpoints.

### 4.2 Retrieve Plaintext Secret
```http
GET /api/v1/projects/:projectId/environments/:environmentId/secrets/:key/value
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
```

### 4.3 Set or Update Secrets (Bulk or Single)
```http
POST /api/v1/projects/:projectId/environments/:environmentId/secrets
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "secrets": [
    { "key": "DATABASE_URL", "value": "postgres://..." },
    { "key": "STRIPE_SECRET_KEY", "value": "sk_live_..." }
  ]
}
```

### 4.4 Delete Secret
```http
DELETE /api/v1/projects/:projectId/environments/:environmentId/secrets/:key
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
```

---

## 5. Developer CLI Workflows (`sem`)

The official CLI automates secret synchronization in local terminal sessions and CI/CD pipelines:

```bash
# Global installation
pnpm add -g @sem/cli

# Authenticate against your SEM instance
sem auth login --host https://sem.niranjansah87.com.np

# Pull secrets to local .env file
sem pull --project backend --env staging --output .env.staging

# Run application with in-memory secrets injection (zero disk persistence)
sem run --project backend --env production -- npm start
```

---

## 6. Self-Hosted Deployment Guide

### Prerequisites
- Node.js 22 LTS
- pnpm 9+
- Docker & Docker Compose
- PostgreSQL 16
- Redis 7

### Installation via Docker Compose

```bash
# 1. Clone repository
git clone https://github.com/niranjansah87/Secure-Enviornment-Manager.git
cd Secure-Enviornment-Manager

# 2. Setup environment and generate keys
cp .env.example .env
pnpm install
pnpm keys:generate

# 3. Launch stack
docker compose -f docker-compose.v2.yml up --build -d
```

Services exposed:
- `api`: NestJS Fastify backend on port 3001 (`/healthz` health check)
- `frontend`: Next.js 15 console on port 3000
- `postgres`: PostgreSQL 16 on port 5432
- `redis`: Redis 7 on port 6379
